nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Plan a three-day offsite for our 12-person remote team next spring
nodes.body:
## Destination
A plan that the ops lead can book from. It gives the dates, the place, the venue, a day-by-day agenda, the budget split and the travel plan.

## Notes
- **Offsite**: the yearly in-person meetup of our fully-remote company. The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America.
- **Strategy session**: the CEO's half-day planning block.
- The total budget is fixed.
- Last year's offsite felt like a conference. Avoid that.
- Everyone must be able to take part.

## Done when
- The dates are fixed.
- The location and the venue type are chosen.
- The team agrees on an agenda skeleton for the 3 days.
- The budget is split per category, within the total.
- The team agrees on the travel approach: who books, and the flight limits.
- Accessibility needs and diet needs are covered.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which region hosts the offsite?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America. We do not yet know how many people live on each side.

**The problem**: Every region makes one group fly long and lose time to jet lag. We must pick who carries that cost.

**What hangs on it**: The venue search, the flight budget, the travel days, and how much of day 1 we lose to jet lag.

options.label: Western Europe, near a big hub (recommended)
options.detail: For example Lisbon or near Amsterdam. Europeans fly 2 to 4 hours. North Americans fly 7 to 10 hours overnight, with direct flights from most big cities. Costs less for the larger group if most people live in Europe.

options.label: East coast of North America
options.detail: For example near New York or Montreal. North Americans fly less. Europeans fly 7 to 9 hours and lose a day to jet lag.

options.label: A midpoint over the Atlantic
options.detail: For example Iceland or the Azores. Both sides fly about the same time. Fewer direct flights, so more connections and higher fares.

options.label: Rotate each year
options.detail: Pick the side that did not host last year. Fair over time, but this year one side carries all the long flights.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: What type of venue do we book?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: Last year's offsite felt like a conference. We want to avoid that. Everyone must be able to take part.

**The problem**: The venue sets the feel more than the agenda does. A hotel conference room pulls toward talks and slides. A shared house pulls toward conversation, but it can fail on accessibility.

**What hangs on it**: The budget split between rooms and food, the agenda, and the accessibility check.

options.label: One rented house or small retreat, for the whole team (recommended)
options.detail: Everyone sleeps, eats and works in one place. It feels the least like a conference. Needs a check for step-free rooms and a big enough work room.

options.label: Boutique hotel with one private meeting room
options.detail: Rooms, food and cleaning come included. Less work for the ops lead. Shared spaces with other guests make it feel more formal.

options.label: City hotel plus a rented work space nearby
options.detail: Easy to reach, many restaurants. Daily transfers, and it is close to last year's conference feel.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How do we split the 3 days between work and social time?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite lasts three days. The CEO's strategy session needs half a day. Last year felt like a conference.

**The problem**: We do not know how much planned work the team wants. Too much feels like a conference. Too little can feel like a lost week.

**What hangs on it**: The agenda skeleton, the activity budget, and the size of the work room we need.

options.label: Mornings work, afternoons free or social (recommended)
options.detail: The strategy session takes one morning. The other mornings are working sessions. Afternoons are for walks, an activity, or rest. Leaves less time for planned work.

options.label: One day each: strategy, work, social
options.detail: Clear structure. A full work day can feel like a conference again.

options.label: Mostly social, strategy session only
options.detail: The strategy session is the only planned work block. Strongest team bonding, but less concrete output.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which spring window do we target?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite is next spring. The team lives in many countries with different public holidays.

**The problem**: Spring is long. Early dates are cheaper but colder. Late dates collide with summer prices. We also must avoid public and school holidays where the team lives.

**What hangs on it**: The venue prices, the outdoor activities in the agenda, and the date poll.

options.label: Mid-May 2027 (recommended)
options.detail: Warm enough for outdoor time in most of Europe. After the Easter break and before the busy summer season. Venue prices start to rise.

options.label: Late April 2027
options.detail: Lower venue prices and fewer tourists. The weather is less certain, so indoor backup plans are needed.

options.label: Early June 2027
options.detail: Best weather. Some venues already charge summer prices, and school holidays start in some countries.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Easter 2027 falls on 28 March
nodes.body:
Easter Sunday 2027 is on 28 March. Many European countries also close on Good Friday (26 March) and Easter Monday (29 March).

Source: computed with the standard Gregorian Easter formula in Python.

My inference: any window in April or later avoids the Easter break. Ascension Day (6 May 2027) and Whit Monday (17 May 2027) are public holidays in several European countries. A mid-May date must check these.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Who books the flights?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The total budget is fixed. People fly from both Europe and North America.

**The problem**: Someone must book about 12 return flights. The choice sets who controls cost and who carries the work.

**What hangs on it**: The flight limits (class, cap, layovers), the travel budget line, and the arrival plan for day 1.

options.label: The ops lead books all flights centrally (recommended)
options.detail: One person sees all costs and arrival times. Easier to hold the budget and group arrivals. More work for the ops lead.

options.label: Each person books, within a fixed cap
options.detail: Less work for the ops lead. People choose their own times and airlines. Harder to coordinate arrivals, and people pay first and claim later.

options.label: A travel agency books for everyone
options.detail: Less work for the ops lead, and help when flights change. Costs an agency fee.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Collect the total budget and each person's home airport
nodes.body:
The ops lead gets two facts:
- The fixed total budget, in one currency.
- Each person's nearest airport.

These facts drive the region choice and the flight cost estimate. They are facts, so no discussion is needed.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Collect accessibility and diet needs privately
nodes.body:
Send a short private form to all 12 people. Ask about:
- Mobility: stairs, walking distance, step-free rooms.
- Diet: allergies, religious or ethical diets.
- Other needs: quiet space, medical needs, childcare or caring duties.

Only the ops lead sees the answers. The venue and agenda choices must check against them.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How we split the fixed budget across categories
nodes.body: The total is fixed. The categories are likely flights, venue and rooms, food, activities, local transport, and a reserve. The split depends on the region and the venue type. We cannot set numbers until those are chosen.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: What made last year feel like a conference
nodes.body: We know last year felt like a conference. We do not know why. Possible causes: talks with slides, a hotel meeting room, a packed schedule, or little free time. Knowing the cause tells us what to change in the agenda and venue.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Flight limits: class, cost cap and layovers
nodes.body: Long flights from North America may need rules: economy or premium economy, a cost cap per person, a maximum number of layovers, and arrival a day early to beat jet lag. The rules depend on the region and the budget.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Ground transport and arrival day
nodes.body: People land at different times. Someone must get them from the airport to the venue. A remote house needs a shuttle or rental cars. A city venue needs only trains or taxis. This depends on the venue type.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Risks: visas, travel insurance and people who cannot travel
nodes.body: Some people may need a visa or a travel authorisation for the chosen country. Some may fall ill or be unable to fly. Everyone must be able to take part, so we may need a plan for people who cannot come in person.

nodes.author: user
nodes.title: Portugal, ideally within an hour of Lisbon airport. Five of the twelve of us live in Lisbon or Porto, so it is the cheapest option by far, and Berlin and Warsaw have direct flights.
nodes.body: My worry is fairness: the two Toronto people and the one in Austin carry all the long flights. I would like to soften that rather than move the whole offsite, for example by letting them arrive a day early on the company.

nodes.author: user
nodes.title: Late April or the first half of May 2027, Tuesday to Thursday so nobody travels on a weekend.
nodes.body: I disagree with mid-May as the default. Two parents cannot do weekends, and one person cannot travel in the last week of May because of a school event. Your note about Ascension (6 May) and Whit Monday (17 May) also argues for avoiding mid-May. Spring prices in Portugal are lower before May anyway.

nodes.author: user
nodes.title: Mornings work, afternoons free or social (recommended)
nodes.body: Tom (our CEO) wants his half-day strategy session, and he can have one morning. The team mostly wants real time together and one memorable activity. Please keep afternoons genuinely optional: two people hated last year's forced fun and should be able to opt out without it being awkward.

nodes.author: user
nodes.title: Budget is €18k all-in; 12 people in 5 cities
nodes.body:
Here are the facts, so we can skip the collection step for the budget part.

- Total budget: €18,000, including all travel. Our CFO is strict, so anything over that needs a written reason.
- Where people live: 5 in Lisbon/Porto, 3 in Berlin, 1 in Warsaw, 2 in Toronto, 1 in Austin.
- Likely home airports: LIS and OPO, BER, WAW, YYZ, and AUS.

That works out to €1,500 per person all-in, which I think is tight but doable if we stay in Portugal.

nodes.author: user
nodes.title: Ana uses a wheelchair: the venue must be step-free
nodes.body:
One fact that matters for the venue choice: Ana, who lives in Lisbon, uses a wheelchair. A rented villa only works if it has step-free access, at least one accessible bedroom and bathroom on the ground floor, and a work room she can reach without stairs. Old Portuguese quintas often fail on this, so we should check it before we fall in love with a place.

I am honestly torn between a whole villa and a hotel. A villa feels more like us, but a good hotel takes the cooking, cleaning and accessibility worries off my plate.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport
nodes.body:
The user settled the region.

- The offsite is in Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport (LIS).
- Reason: five of the twelve people live in Lisbon or Porto. Berlin and Warsaw have direct flights. This is the cheapest choice by far.
- The two people from Toronto and the one from Austin carry the long flights. We soften this for them. We do not move the offsite.

How we soften it is open, in "How do we soften the long flights for Toronto and Austin?".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How do we soften the long flights for Toronto and Austin?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite is in Portugal, near Lisbon (see "Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport"). Two people fly from Toronto (YYZ) and one from Austin (AUS). They carry all the long flights. You want to soften this, for example with a paid extra day before the offsite.

**The problem**: Each way to soften it costs money from the fixed 18,000 euro budget. Also, a flight from Toronto that lands in Lisbon on Monday morning leaves on Sunday evening. So the North Americans travel on a weekend, even if the Europeans do not. Austin probably has no direct flight to Lisbon, so that trip takes one stop (not checked yet).

**What hangs on it**: The flight limits, the number of room nights we pay for, and the arrival plan for day 1.

options.label: Arrive one day early, extra night paid by the company (recommended)
options.detail: They land the day before the others and rest. Costs about 3 extra room nights plus meals, roughly 300 to 500 euros in total (my estimate). They travel one day more.

options.label: Premium economy on the long flights
options.detail: They sleep better on the flight but arrive on the same day as the others. Costs roughly 500 to 1,000 euros more per person (my estimate), so 1,500 to 3,000 euros. Needs a written reason for the CFO.

options.label: Arrive one day early and stay one day after, both on the company
options.detail: Two rest days and less pressure on flight times. Costs about 6 extra room nights plus meals, roughly 600 to 1,000 euros (my estimate).

options.label: Same travel rules as everyone else
options.detail: Cheapest. The fairness problem stays as it is.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Dates: late April or first half of May 2027, Tuesday to Thursday
nodes.body:
The user settled the date window.

- The offsite runs Tuesday to Thursday, so nobody travels on a weekend.
- The window is late April to the first half of May 2027.
- Mid-May is not the default any more. Reasons from the user:
  - Two parents cannot travel on weekends.
  - One person cannot travel in the last week of May (school event).
  - Ascension Day (6 May) and Whit Monday (17 May) are public holidays in several European countries.
  - Spring prices in Portugal are lower before May.

The exact week is open. See "Three candidate weeks: 20-22 April, 27-29 April, 11-13 May".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Three candidate weeks: 20-22 April, 27-29 April, 11-13 May
nodes.body:
Tuesday-to-Thursday weeks in the window, checked against public holidays where the team lives:

- **20-22 April 2027**: no clash found.
- **27-29 April 2027**: no clash found. Portugal's Freedom Day (25 April) is a Sunday.
- **4-6 May 2027**: excluded. Thursday 6 May is Ascension Day, a public holiday in Germany. Monday 3 May is a public holiday in Poland (Constitution Day), which is the travel day.
- **11-13 May 2027**: no clash found. Whit Monday (17 May) falls in the week after.

Labour Day (1 May 2027) is a Saturday, so it does not clash.

Source: weekdays computed with the Python calendar. Ascension (Easter + 39 days) and Whit Monday (Easter + 50 days) come from Easter on 28 March 2027, see "Easter 2027 falls on 28 March". The fixed holidays are the national holidays of Portugal, Germany and Poland.

Not checked: school holidays in Berlin, Warsaw, Toronto and Austin, and local holidays in Lisbon and Porto.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Run a date poll for the three candidate weeks
nodes.body:
The ops lead sends one short poll to all 12 people. It lists the three candidate weeks:

- 20-22 April 2027
- 27-29 April 2027
- 11-13 May 2027

Each person marks the weeks they can do. They can also mark school holidays that we did not check. Pick the week that everyone can do. If there is a tie, pick the earliest week, because prices are lower before May.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How many nights at the venue does the company pay for?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite runs Tuesday to Thursday (see "Dates: late April or first half of May 2027, Tuesday to Thursday"). Mornings are for work, afternoons are optional. We hire a small country hotel or wine estate near Lisbon. I assume all 12 people sleep at the venue, also the 5 from Lisbon and Porto, because time together is the point.

**The problem**: "Tuesday to Thursday" says which days we work. It does not say when people arrive and leave. A "night" here is one person in one room for one night. Rooms are the largest cost after flights. For example, 4 nights cost about twice as much as 2 nights.

The Toronto and Austin people arrive one day earlier than the rest (see "Toronto and Austin arrive one day early, on the company"). That extra night comes on top of every option below. With 4 nights, they land on Sunday, so they fly on Saturday night.

**What hangs on it**: The venue quote we ask for, the money left for food and the activity, the arrival plan, and whether Tuesday morning is a full working morning.

options.label: 4 nights: arrive Monday evening, leave Friday morning (recommended)
options.detail: All three days are full days, and the Thursday afternoon stays free. Costs the most: 48 room nights for 12 people.

options.label: 3 nights: arrive Monday evening, leave Thursday evening
options.detail: Saves 12 room nights. The Thursday afternoon is lost to travel. Toronto and Austin have no evening flights home, so those 3 people still need a fourth night.

options.label: 2 nights: arrive Tuesday morning, leave Thursday evening
options.detail: Cheapest: 24 room nights. Everyone takes an early flight on Tuesday, so the Tuesday working morning is lost or starts late.

history.title: Which nights at the venue do we pay for?
history.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite runs Tuesday to Thursday (see "Dates: late April or first half of May 2027, Tuesday to Thursday"). The agenda puts work in the mornings. I assume all 12 people sleep at the venue, also the people from Lisbon, because time together is the point.

**The problem**: "Tuesday to Thursday" does not yet say when people arrive and leave. The number of nights is the largest cost after flights. For example, 4 nights cost about twice as much as 2 nights.

**What hangs on it**: The venue budget, the venue search, the arrival plan, and whether the Tuesday morning is a working morning.

options.label: Arrive Monday evening, leave Friday morning: 4 nights (recommended)
options.detail: Three full days, and travel only on Monday and Friday. Costs the most room nights: 4 nights for the whole group.

options.label: Arrive Monday evening, leave Thursday evening: 3 nights
options.detail: Saves one night for everyone. Thursday afternoon goes to travel. Return flights to North America leave in daytime, so those three still need a Friday flight and a fourth night.

options.label: Arrive Tuesday morning, leave Thursday evening: 2 nights
options.detail: Cheapest. Everyone takes an early flight on Tuesday, so the Tuesday working morning is lost.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Agenda: work in the mornings, afternoons optional
nodes.body:
The user settled the shape of the three days.

- **Mornings are for work.** One morning is the strategy session of Tom, our CEO. The other two mornings are working sessions.
- **Afternoons are free or social, and truly optional.** Anyone can opt out of an afternoon plan without giving a reason. Two people disliked the forced social activities last year.
- **One memorable activity.** The team mostly wants real time together and one activity they will remember.

Open: what the activity is and how the opt-out works. See "The one memorable activity".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: The one memorable activity
nodes.body: The team wants one memorable activity in an afternoon. We do not know yet what it is. It must be optional, so people who skip it do not feel left out. It must also be step-free, so Ana can take part. It costs money from the activity line of the budget. It depends on the venue and the season: for example a boat trip on the Tagus, a cooking class, or a day at the coast.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Budget is 18,000 euros all-in; home airports are known
nodes.body:
The user gave the budget and the home airports, so the collection task is done.

- **Total budget**: 18,000 euros, including all travel. That is 1,500 euros per person. Anything over the total needs a written reason for the CFO.
- **Where people live, and their airports**:
  - 5 in Lisbon or Porto: LIS, OPO
  - 3 in Berlin: BER
  - 1 in Warsaw: WAW
  - 2 in Toronto: YYZ
  - 1 in Austin: AUS

The accessibility and diet needs are still collected separately, in "Collect accessibility and diet needs privately".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Flights take roughly 3,000 to 5,000 euros of the budget
nodes.body:
My inference. These are rough return-fare ranges in economy. I did not check live prices.

| From | People | Each | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lisbon or Porto (train or local) | 5 | 0-70 | 50-200 |
| Berlin (direct) | 3 | 150-300 | 450-900 |
| Warsaw (direct) | 1 | 200-350 | 200-350 |
| Toronto (direct) | 2 | 700-1,000 | 1,400-2,000 |
| Austin (one stop) | 1 | 900-1,400 | 900-1,400 |
| **All** | 12 | | **3,000-4,850** |

So about 13,000 to 15,000 euros remain for the venue, food, the activity, local transport and a reserve. That is about 1,100 to 1,250 euros per person.

With a strict CFO, a reserve of about 10% (1,800 euros) protects against price changes. The split per category stays open until the venue type and the number of nights are chosen. See "Which nights at the venue do we pay for?".

nodes.title: The venue must be step-free for Ana

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Venue research: few accessible options found, no spring prices
nodes.body:
Research for "What type of venue do we book?". The search was limited: web search engines blocked the lookup, so I could read only venue sites I already knew. I found no spring 2027 prices for any venue type.

**Venues found near Lisbon (facts from their own sites)**
- **Areias do Seixo**, Silver Coast, about 45-50 minutes by car (my estimate). Boutique hotel with suites and villas. It hosts small meetings and retreats. Accessibility, room count and price are not stated. https://www.areiasdoseixo.com/en/events
- **Quinta de Sant'Ana**, Gradil, Mafra. Wine estate with guest houses and space for team events. Capacity, accessibility and price are not stated. https://www.quintadesantana.com/
- **Vila Galé Ericeira**. Large hotel, 202 rooms and 11 meeting rooms, but only one room for reduced mobility. It is close to a conference hotel. https://www.vilagale.com/en/hotels/lisbon-region/vila-gale-ericeira
- **A whole villa for 12 with an accessible ground floor**: none found.

**How to check accessibility**
- TUR4all lists accessible hotels, restaurants and transport in Portugal. https://www.tur4all.com/resources/search
- Accessible Portugal does accessibility consulting and plans accessible group trips. https://accessibleportugal.com/
- Sintra's parks say their sites are still being adapted, and access differs per site. https://www.parquesdesintra.pt/en/plan-your-visit/accessibility/

**My inference**
- A hotel can have only one adapted room. Confirm that this room is held for our dates.
- A middle way exists between the two options you are torn between: hire a small country hotel or wine estate for the whole group alone. It feels like a house, but the staff cook and clean, and it is easier to find one built to current access rules.
- Ask each venue for door widths of the bedroom, bathroom and work room, a roll-in shower with no lip, threshold heights, and photos of the route from parking with a tape measure in shot.

Next step: email Areias do Seixo and Quinta de Sant'Ana for capacity, access photos and a quote for April or May 2027.

nodes.body:

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Ask candidate venues for a whole-place quote and access proof
nodes.body:
The ops lead emails 3 to 5 small country hotels or wine estates within one hour of Lisbon airport. Start with Areias do Seixo and Quinta de Sant'Ana, from "Venue research: few accessible options found, no spring prices". Use TUR4all (https://www.tur4all.com/resources/search) to find more.

Ask each venue:
- Can we hire the whole place for 12 people, for each of the three candidate weeks?
- A price for 2, 3 and 4 nights, with breakfast, lunch and dinner. This lets us compare the options in "How many nights at the venue does the company pay for?".
- A meeting room for 12 that is free every morning.
- Proof of step-free access: door widths of the bedroom, bathroom and work room, a roll-in shower with no lip, threshold heights, and photos of the route from parking with a tape measure in shot.
- Whether they hold their adapted room for us, and whether they arrange airport transfers.

Keep the boutique hotel fallback on the list, in case no whole place is free.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Flights: the ops lead books all 12 centrally, in one fare sheet
nodes.body:
The user settled who books the flights.

- The ops lead books all 12 return trips. The ops lead has done this before.
- Every fare goes into one spreadsheet: person, route, dates, fare, and fare rules. The CFO gets this sheet.
- The 5 people from Lisbon and Porto may need only a train ticket or nothing. They go in the same sheet, so the travel total is complete.

Still open: the fare rules the ops lead books by. See "Which fare rules do the flights follow?".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Toronto and Austin arrive one day early, on the company
nodes.body:
The user settled how we soften the long flights.

- The 2 people from Toronto and the 1 from Austin arrive one day before the others. The company pays the extra night and meals. My earlier estimate: 300 to 500 euros in total.
- **Austin only**: if the return trip from Austin has a long layover, the ops lead may add one night after the offsite. This is a choice at booking time, not a rule. Toronto does not get a night after.
- No premium economy.

This extra night comes on top of the nights in "How many nights at the venue does the company pay for?".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: The reserve comes out of the 18,000: about 900 to 1,100 euros per person remain
nodes.body:
Reply to "Does the 10% reserve come on top of the category split?". Yes, the reserve comes out of the money that remains after flights. The 18,000 euros is all-in (see "Budget is 18,000 euros all-in; home airports are known"), so nothing can sit next to it.

My calculation, from the numbers already on the map:

| Line | Low case | High case |
|---|---|---|
| Total budget | 18,000 | 18,000 |
| Reserve, 10% | -1,800 | -1,800 |
| Flights (from "Flights take roughly 3,000 to 5,000 euros of the budget") | -4,850 | -3,000 |
| **Left for venue, food, activity, local transport** | **11,350** | **13,200** |
| **Per person** | **about 950** | **about 1,100** |
| Early night for Toronto and Austin | -500 | -300 |
| **Left after the early night** | **10,850** | **12,900** |
| **Per person** | **about 900** | **about 1,075** |

So your figure is right. The figure for the CFO is about 900 to 1,075 euros per person, for rooms, all meals, the activity and local transport.

Per person per night, that is about:
- 4 nights: 225 to 270 euros;
- 3 nights: 300 to 360 euros;
- 2 nights: 450 to 540 euros.

The low case uses the high flight prices. The flight numbers are my estimates, not live prices. The venue quotes will show which night count fits.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which fare rules do the flights follow?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The ops lead books all 12 trips (see "Flights: the ops lead books all 12 centrally, in one fare sheet"). The travel budget is about 3,000 to 5,000 euros. Toronto and Austin arrive one day early. Nobody flies premium economy.

**The problem**: Fares of the same class differ a lot in what they allow. The cheapest fares often have no checked bag and no changes. The booking date is about 5 to 6 months before the offsite. In that time, someone can fall ill or have a family event. A central booker needs one rule for all fares, so the CFO sees one clear policy. With a central booker, a cost cap per person is less important: the cap is the fare range in the flight estimate, and the ops lead explains any fare above it.

Layovers: I suggest at most one stop on every route. Only Austin needs one.

**What hangs on it**: The flight total, how much of the reserve stays free, and the plan in "Risks: visas, travel insurance and people who cannot travel".

options.label: Economy with one checked bag and a free date change (recommended)
options.detail: A person who falls ill can move the trip, not lose it. Costs more than the cheapest fare, maybe 10 to 20% (my estimate), so about 300 to 900 euros for the group.

options.label: The cheapest economy fare, no changes
options.detail: Lowest cost, fits the fare estimate best. If someone cannot travel, the fare is lost, and the reserve pays for any new ticket.

options.label: Fully refundable fares

nodes.title: Why the Lisbon region could fail, and the strongest alternative
nodes.body:
Reply to the challenge on "Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport". All of this is my inference. I assume the offsite took place in April 2027 and went badly, and ask why.

**The strongest reasons it failed**
1. **No venue passed every test.** The place must be within one hour, hired whole, step-free with a real roll-in shower, and able to cook vegan meals. The earlier research found no whole place that is confirmed step-free (see "Venue research: few accessible options found, no spring prices"). The one-hour limit is the easiest test to relax, but nobody had agreed to relax it, so we fell back to a hotel that felt like a conference again.
2. **It did not feel like an offsite for the 5 locals.** They can sleep at home on Monday and stay close to home tasks. The group was not together from the start.
3. **The long flights still hurt.** Toronto is a long direct flight, and Austin needs a stop. One early night helps with jet lag, but those 3 people still spent the most time and energy.
4. **Arrival went wrong.** Lisbon airport is busy and delays are common. A minibus at fixed times waits, or leaves people behind.

**The strongest alternative**: keep Portugal, but allow up to 90 minutes from the airport if no venue within one hour passes the access check. This opens areas such as the Alentejo coast, Comporta or Óbidos (my examples, not checked for venues). It keeps the cost advantage that made Portugal the choice. A different country gives up that advantage, and no reason on the map calls for it.

Reasons 2 to 4 are already handled in part, by "Venue nights: 51 room nights, Monday 26 to Friday 30 April" and "Airport transfer: one booked minibus, taxis outside its times, two choices kept for Ana". Reason 1 needs a choice from you, in "If no venue within one hour passes the access check, what do we relax first?".

|---|---|---|---|

## Destination
A plan that the ops lead can book from. It gives the dates, the place, the venue, a day-by-day agenda, the budget split and the travel plan.

## Notes
- **Offsite**: the yearly in-person meetup of our fully-remote company. The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America.
- **Strategy session**: the CEO's half-day planning block.
- The total budget is fixed.
- Last year's offsite felt like a conference. Avoid that.
- Everyone must be able to take part.

## Done when
- The dates are fixed.
- The location and the venue type are chosen.
- The team agrees on an agenda skeleton for the 3 days.
- The budget is split per category, within the total.
- The team agrees on the travel approach: who books, and the flight limits.
- Accessibility needs and diet needs are covered.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which region hosts the offsite?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America. We do not yet know how many people live on each side.

**The problem**: Every region makes one group fly long and lose time to jet lag. We must pick who carries that cost.

**What hangs on it**: The venue search, the flight budget, the travel days, and how much of day 1 we lose to jet lag.

options.label: Western Europe, near a big hub (recommended)
options.detail: For example Lisbon or near Amsterdam. Europeans fly 2 to 4 hours. North Americans fly 7 to 10 hours overnight, with direct flights from most big cities. Costs less for the larger group if most people live in Europe.

options.label: East coast of North America
options.detail: For example near New York or Montreal. North Americans fly less. Europeans fly 7 to 9 hours and lose a day to jet lag.

options.label: A midpoint over the Atlantic
options.detail: For example Iceland or the Azores. Both sides fly about the same time. Fewer direct flights, so more connections and higher fares.

options.label: Rotate each year
options.detail: Pick the side that did not host last year. Fair over time, but this year one side carries all the long flights.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: What type of venue do we book?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: Last year's offsite felt like a conference. We want to avoid that. Everyone must be able to take part.

**The problem**: The venue sets the feel more than the agenda does. A hotel conference room pulls toward talks and slides. A shared house pulls toward conversation, but it can fail on accessibility.

**What hangs on it**: The budget split between rooms and food, the agenda, and the accessibility check.

options.label: One rented house or small retreat, for the whole team (recommended)
options.detail: Everyone sleeps, eats and works in one place. It feels the least like a conference. Needs a check for step-free rooms and a big enough work room.

options.label: Boutique hotel with one private meeting room
options.detail: Rooms, food and cleaning come included. Less work for the ops lead. Shared spaces with other guests make it feel more formal.

options.label: City hotel plus a rented work space nearby
options.detail: Easy to reach, many restaurants. Daily transfers, and it is close to last year's conference feel.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How do we split the 3 days between work and social time?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite lasts three days. The CEO's strategy session needs half a day. Last year felt like a conference.

**The problem**: We do not know how much planned work the team wants. Too much feels like a conference. Too little can feel like a lost week.

**What hangs on it**: The agenda skeleton, the activity budget, and the size of the work room we need.

options.label: Mornings work, afternoons free or social (recommended)
options.detail: The strategy session takes one morning. The other mornings are working sessions. Afternoons are for walks, an activity, or rest. Leaves less time for planned work.

options.label: One day each: strategy, work, social
options.detail: Clear structure. A full work day can feel like a conference again.

options.label: Mostly social, strategy session only
options.detail: The strategy session is the only planned work block. Strongest team bonding, but less concrete output.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which spring window do we target?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite is next spring. The team lives in many countries with different public holidays.

**The problem**: Spring is long. Early dates are cheaper but colder. Late dates collide with summer prices. We also must avoid public and school holidays where the team lives.

**What hangs on it**: The venue prices, the outdoor activities in the agenda, and the date poll.

options.label: Mid-May 2027 (recommended)
options.detail: Warm enough for outdoor time in most of Europe. After the Easter break and before the busy summer season. Venue prices start to rise.

options.label: Late April 2027
options.detail: Lower venue prices and fewer tourists. The weather is less certain, so indoor backup plans are needed.

options.label: Early June 2027
options.detail: Best weather. Some venues already charge summer prices, and school holidays start in some countries.

nodes.title: Why the Lisbon region could fail, and the strongest alternative
nodes.body:
Reply to the challenge on "Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport". All of this is my inference. I assume the offsite took place in April 2027 and went badly, and ask why.

**The strongest reasons it failed**
1. **No venue passed every test.** The place must be within one hour, hired whole, step-free with a real roll-in shower, and able to cook vegan meals. The earlier research found no whole place that is confirmed step-free (see "Venue research: few accessible options found, no spring prices"). The one-hour limit is the easiest test to relax, but nobody had agreed to relax it, so we fell back to a hotel that felt like a conference again.
2. **It did not feel like an offsite for the 5 locals.** They can sleep at home on Monday and stay close to home tasks. The group was not together from the start.
3. **The long flights still hurt.** Toronto is a long direct flight, and Austin needs a stop. One early night helps with jet lag, but those 3 people still spent the most time and energy.
4. **Arrival went wrong.** Lisbon airport is busy and delays are common. A minibus at fixed times waits, or leaves people behind.

**The strongest alternative**: keep Portugal, but allow up to 90 minutes from the airport if no venue within one hour passes the access check. This opens areas such as the Alentejo coast, Comporta or Óbidos (my examples, not checked for venues). It keeps the cost advantage that made Portugal the choice. A different country gives up that advantage, and no reason on the map calls for it.

Reasons 2 to 4 are already handled in part, by "Venue nights: 51 room nights, Monday 26 to Friday 30 April" and "Airport transfer: one booked minibus, taxis outside its times, two choices kept for Ana". Reason 1 needs a choice from you, in "If no venue within one hour passes the access check, what do we relax first?".

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Plan a three-day offsite for our 12-person remote team next spring
nodes.body:
## Destination
A plan that the ops lead can book from. It gives the dates, the place, the venue, a day-by-day agenda, the budget split and the travel plan.

## Notes
- **Offsite**: the yearly in-person meetup of our fully-remote company. The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America.
- **Strategy session**: the CEO's half-day planning block.
- The total budget is fixed.
- Last year's offsite felt like a conference. Avoid that.
- Everyone must be able to take part.

## Done when
- The dates are fixed.
- The location and the venue type are chosen.
- The team agrees on an agenda skeleton for the 3 days.
- The budget is split per category, within the total.
- The team agrees on the travel approach: who books, and the flight limits.
- Accessibility needs and diet needs are covered.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which region hosts the offsite?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The team of 12 lives across Europe and North America. We do not yet know how many people live on each side.

**The problem**: Every region makes one group fly long and lose time to jet lag. We must pick who carries that cost.

**What hangs on it**: The venue search, the flight budget, the travel days, and how much of day 1 we lose to jet lag.

options.label: Western Europe, near a big hub (recommended)
options.detail: For example Lisbon or near Amsterdam. Europeans fly 2 to 4 hours. North Americans fly 7 to 10 hours overnight, with direct flights from most big cities. Costs less for the larger group if most people live in Europe.

options.label: East coast of North America
options.detail: For example near New York or Montreal. North Americans fly less. Europeans fly 7 to 9 hours and lose a day to jet lag.

options.label: A midpoint over the Atlantic
options.detail: For example Iceland or the Azores. Both sides fly about the same time. Fewer direct flights, so more connections and higher fares.

options.label: Rotate each year
options.detail: Pick the side that did not host last year. Fair over time, but this year one side carries all the long flights.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: What type of venue do we book?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: Last year's offsite felt like a conference. We want to avoid that. Everyone must be able to take part.

**The problem**: The venue sets the feel more than the agenda does. A hotel conference room pulls toward talks and slides. A shared house pulls toward conversation, but it can fail on accessibility.

**What hangs on it**: The budget split between rooms and food, the agenda, and the accessibility check.

options.label: One rented house or small retreat, for the whole team (recommended)
options.detail: Everyone sleeps, eats and works in one place. It feels the least like a conference. Needs a check for step-free rooms and a big enough work room.

options.label: Boutique hotel with one private meeting room
options.detail: Rooms, food and cleaning come included. Less work for the ops lead. Shared spaces with other guests make it feel more formal.

options.label: City hotel plus a rented work space nearby
options.detail: Easy to reach, many restaurants. Daily transfers, and it is close to last year's conference feel.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How do we split the 3 days between work and social time?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite lasts three days. The CEO's strategy session needs half a day. Last year felt like a conference.

**The problem**: We do not know how much planned work the team wants. Too much feels like a conference. Too little can feel like a lost week.

**What hangs on it**: The agenda skeleton, the activity budget, and the size of the work room we need.

options.label: Mornings work, afternoons free or social (recommended)
options.detail: The strategy session takes one morning. The other mornings are working sessions. Afternoons are for walks, an activity, or rest. Leaves less time for planned work.

options.label: One day each: strategy, work, social
options.detail: Clear structure. A full work day can feel like a conference again.

options.label: Mostly social, strategy session only
options.detail: The strategy session is the only planned work block. Strongest team bonding, but less concrete output.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Which spring window do we target?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite is next spring. The team lives in many countries with different public holidays.

**The problem**: Spring is long. Early dates are cheaper but colder. Late dates collide with summer prices. We also must avoid public and school holidays where the team lives.

**What hangs on it**: The venue prices, the outdoor activities in the agenda, and the date poll.

options.label: Mid-May 2027 (recommended)
options.detail: Warm enough for outdoor time in most of Europe. After the Easter break and before the busy summer season. Venue prices start to rise.

options.label: Late April 2027
options.detail: Lower venue prices and fewer tourists. The weather is less certain, so indoor backup plans are needed.

options.label: Early June 2027
options.detail: Best weather. Some venues already charge summer prices, and school holidays start in some countries.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Easter 2027 falls on 28 March
nodes.body:
Easter Sunday 2027 is on 28 March. Many European countries also close on Good Friday (26 March) and Easter Monday (29 March).

Source: computed with the standard Gregorian Easter formula in Python.

My inference: any window in April or later avoids the Easter break. Ascension Day (6 May 2027) and Whit Monday (17 May 2027) are public holidays in several European countries. A mid-May date must check these.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Who books the flights?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The total budget is fixed. People fly from both Europe and North America.

**The problem**: Someone must book about 12 return flights. The choice sets who controls cost and who carries the work.

**What hangs on it**: The flight limits (class, cap, layovers), the travel budget line, and the arrival plan for day 1.

options.label: The ops lead books all flights centrally (recommended)
options.detail: One person sees all costs and arrival times. Easier to hold the budget and group arrivals. More work for the ops lead.

options.label: Each person books, within a fixed cap
options.detail: Less work for the ops lead. People choose their own times and airlines. Harder to coordinate arrivals, and people pay first and claim later.

options.label: A travel agency books for everyone
options.detail: Less work for the ops lead, and help when flights change. Costs an agency fee.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Collect the total budget and each person's home airport
nodes.body:
The ops lead gets two facts:
- The fixed total budget, in one currency.
- Each person's nearest airport.

These facts drive the region choice and the flight cost estimate. They are facts, so no discussion is needed.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Collect accessibility and diet needs privately
nodes.body:
Send a short private form to all 12 people. Ask about:
- Mobility: stairs, walking distance, step-free rooms.
- Diet: allergies, religious or ethical diets.
- Other needs: quiet space, medical needs, childcare or caring duties.

Only the ops lead sees the answers. The venue and agenda choices must check against them.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: How we split the fixed budget across categories
nodes.body: The total is fixed. The categories are likely flights, venue and rooms, food, activities, local transport, and a reserve. The split depends on the region and the venue type. We cannot set numbers until those are chosen.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: What made last year feel like a conference
nodes.body: We know last year felt like a conference. We do not know why. Possible causes: talks with slides, a hotel meeting room, a packed schedule, or little free time. Knowing the cause tells us what to change in the agenda and venue.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Flight limits: class, cost cap and layovers
nodes.body: Long flights from North America may need rules: economy or premium economy, a cost cap per person, a maximum number of layovers, and arrival a day early to beat jet lag. The rules depend on the region and the budget.

nodes.author: agent
nodes.title: Ground transport and arrival day
nodes.body: People land at different times. Someone must get them from the airport to the venue. A remote house needs a shuttle or rental cars. A city venue needs only trains or taxis. This depends on the venue type.

nodes.title: Risks: visas, travel insurance and people who cannot travel
nodes.body: Some people may need a visa or a travel authorisation for the chosen country. Some may fall ill or be unable to fly. Everyone must be able to take part, so we may need a plan for people who cannot come in person.

nodes.title: How do we soften the long flights for Toronto and Austin?
nodes.body:
**Where we are**: The offsite is in Portugal, near Lisbon (see "Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport"). Two people fly from Toronto (YYZ) and one from Austin (AUS). They carry all the long flights. You want to soften this, for example with a paid extra day before the offsite.

options.label: Arrive one day early and stay one day after, both on the company
options.detail: Two rest days and less pressure on flight times. Costs about 6 extra room nights plus meals, roughly 600 to 1,000 euros (my estimate).

options.label: Same travel rules as everyone else

nodes.body:
Reply to the challenge on "Region: Portugal, within one hour of Lisbon airport". All of this is my inference. I assume the offsite took place in April 2027 and went badly, and ask why.

**The strongest reasons it failed**
1. **No venue passed every test.** The place must be within one hour, hired whole, step-free with a real roll-in shower, and able to cook vegan meals. The earlier research found no whole place that is confirmed step-free (see "Venue research: few accessible options found, no spring prices"). The one-hour limit is the easiest test to relax, but nobody had agreed to relax it, so we fell back to a hotel that felt like a conference again.
2. **It did not feel like an offsite for the 5 locals.** They can sleep at home on Monday and stay close to home tasks. The group was not together from the start.
3. **The long flights still hurt.** Toronto is a long direct flight, and Austin needs a stop. One early night helps with jet lag, but those 3 people still spent the most time and energy.
4. **Arrival went wrong.** Lisbon airport is busy and delays are common. A minibus at fixed times waits, or leaves people behind.

**The strongest alternative**: keep Portugal, but allow up to 90 minutes from the airport if no venue within one hour passes the access check. This opens areas such as the Alentejo coast, Comporta or Óbidos (my examples, not checked for venues). It keeps the cost advantage that made Portugal the choice. A different country gives up that advantage, and no reason on the map calls for it.

Reasons 2 to 4 are already handled in part, by "Venue nights: 51 room nights, Monday 26 to Friday 30 April" and "Airport transfer: one booked minibus, taxis outside its times, two choices kept for Ana". Reason 1 needs a choice from you, in "If no venue within one hour passes the access check, what do we relax first?".
